name: PSEG Long Island Heat Pump Rebates
summary: Explore rebates for qualifying heat-pump projects through PSEG Long Island.

verified_requirements.description: A participating contractor is required for rebate eligibility.
The equipment must meet the requirements for the applicable heat-pump project.
Project-specific requirements apply, including sizing and controls where required.
Income-based rebate tiers require the program's income-verification process.

eligibility_note: This resource matches your topic. Your rebate eligibility has not been assessed.
next_step: Review the official requirements and discuss your project with a participating contractor.

name: Lighting and Electronics Energy Guide
summary: Explore information about lighting and electronics electricity use, including typical wattages and energy-management options.
change_levels: Easy changes I can do now
eligibility_note: This is an educational resource, not a rebate offer or an eligibility assessment.
next_step: Review the lighting and electronics sections for information relevant to the equipment you use.

name: Whole House Energy Assessment
summary: Explore a home energy assessment to identify drafts, insulation problems, and opportunities to improve comfort and efficiency.
concerns: Drafts or rooms that feel too hot or cold
eligibility_note: Assessment availability and any upgrade incentives must be confirmed with the program. This app has not checked whether you qualify.
next_step: Review the assessment process and contractor options. If you rent, discuss arranging an assessment with your landlord or property manager.

name: Talk to a Local Energy Advisor
provider: Long Island Regional Clean Energy Hub
summary: Get free guidance on home energy efficiency and help understanding energy programs serving Nassau and Suffolk residents.
concerns: Drafts or rooms that feel too hot or cold
eligibility_note: Advisors can explain available programs. Matching this resource does not mean you qualify for a particular incentive.
next_step: Contact a Community Energy Advisor, describe your concern, and ask whether any current programs or incentives are relevant to your situation.

name: Electric Heat-Pump Water Heaters
summary: Learn about electric heat-pump water heaters and explore rebates for eligible equipment.
eligibility_note: This resource covers electric water-heating upgrades, not general water conservation. Customer, equipment, and installation requirements must be checked with the program.
next_step: Review the official equipment and rebate requirements before buying anything. If you rent or cannot approve equipment changes, discuss the option with whoever can.

name: Simple Ways to Save Water
summary: Find practical tips for spotting leaks, using less water, and reducing hot-water waste at home.
change_levels: Easy changes I can do now
eligibility_note: This is general water-saving guidance, not a rebate offer. Ask the property owner or manager before changing fixtures you do not control.
next_step: Start with one everyday habit, such as turning off the tap while brushing your teeth. Check for visible drips and report leaks you cannot safely address.

name: Everyday Appliance Energy-Saving Tips
summary: Explore practical ways to use less energy when doing laundry, washing dishes, cooking, and using electronics.
change_levels: Easy changes I can do now
eligibility_note: These are general appliance-use tips, not a rebate offer. Savings from shifting use to off-peak hours depend on your electricity rate plan.
next_step: Choose one change that fits your home, such as washing clothes in cold water or using your dishwasher's air-dry setting. Check your rate plan before relying on off-peak pricing.

name: Understand Drafts Around Windows and Doors
summary: Learn how air leaks around windows and doors can affect comfort and home energy use.
concerns: Drafts or rooms that feel too hot or cold
change_levels: Easy changes I can do now
eligibility_note: This is educational guidance, not a rebate offer or a recommendation to replace windows. Ask the property owner or manager before modifying fixtures you do not control.
next_step: On the linked page, find the Air Leaks section under Other Tips. Note where you notice drafts around accessible windows and doors, and share those observations with the person responsible for repairs.

name: Everyday Heating and Cooling Tips
summary: Explore everyday heating and cooling guidance, including thermostat use, window coverings, and air-conditioning filters.
change_levels: Easy changes I can do now
eligibility_note: This is general energy-saving guidance, not a rebate offer or a diagnosis of a heating or cooling problem. Only adjust controls or maintain equipment you are permitted to use, and follow the equipment manufacturer's instructions.
next_step: Find the heating and cooling sections and choose one tip that fits your home and the controls you can access. If you cannot adjust the equipment, use the guidance to prepare questions for the person responsible.

name: Compare Appliances Using the EnergyGuide Label
summary: Learn how to compare similar appliances using the EnergyGuide label's estimated energy use and yearly operating costs.
eligibility_note: This is appliance-comparison guidance, not a rebate offer or a recommendation to replace an appliance. Label operating costs are estimates based on typical use and national average energy prices; your actual costs may differ.
next_step: If replacement is worth exploring, compare the EnergyGuide labels for similar appliance models. Review estimated energy use and operating costs alongside the purchase price. Labels may be available on the appliance or the seller's or manufacturer's website. Confirm permission before replacing equipment you do not control.

name: REAP: Income-Eligible Home Energy Assistance
summary: Explore an income-qualified home energy survey, personalized energy-use guidance, and possible installation of energy-saving measures such as LED bulbs and water-conservation devices.

verified_requirements.description: A PSEG Long Island account must be in your name.
Household income must meet the program's current guidelines, and proof of income is required.
You must not have had a REAP Home Energy Survey within the past five years.

eligibility_note: Both renters and homeowners may participate if program requirements are met. This app has not checked your eligibility. Installed measures depend on the program's assessment; REAP no longer offers appliance evaluations.
next_step: Review the current income guidelines and account requirements on the official page. If they appear to fit your household, follow the instructions to schedule a survey. Confirm any property-owner approval needed for installed measures.
